summary: 1940 CCC-built 68-foot steel lookout on Coot Mountain, Shannon County, Missouri; standing and Department-owned, with a gate that a trail listing says is often locked.

facts.design: 68-foot steel tower with a 7 x 7 foot cab, plus a cabin and garage that appear younger than the tower

access.note: A trail-app listing says the service gate is likely closed and locked, with a 0.2-mile hike to the tower. No official visiting rule was found.

visit.trail_note: Shannon County Road 216 is gravel from Missouri Route V. The trail listing puts a 0.2-mile hike past the gate to the tower.

corrections.why: The 20.4 m brief value matches the 67-foot figure from the 1939 pre-construction note. The 1940 completion entry gives a 68-foot steel tower (about 20.7 m), and the onX listing also says 68 feet.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Register and the Forest Lookouts page both give 1940. The Register credits the CCC. An onX listing, citing MDC, says a wooden tower came in 1939 and was rebuilt as steel in 1967. The story reports the rebuild as unconfirmed.
The 1939 note gives 67 feet, the 1940 completion entry gives 68 feet, and the onX listing gives 68 feet. The record uses 68 feet (20.7 m).

notes_for_editor: Fact-check 2026-10-09: the Register and Forest Lookouts pages were searched for 'rebuil', 'wood' and '1967' and show no rebuild, so the story keeps the onX account as unconfirmed. The 1940 build date and the 68-foot steel tower agree across the Register and Forest Lookouts. The wood-then-steel rebuild in 1967 rests on one trail-app listing that cites MDC; I could not reach MDC's own page on it, so it is marked unconfirmed. Access is 'restricted' based on a trail listing that says the gate is likely closed and locked; no official visiting rule was found. No tower-specific staffing record was found, and the MDC magazine's staffing lines are general to its towers. The brief's 20.4 m height is corrected to 20.7 m (68 ft). The NGS 1962 station note calls the overall height approximately 80 feet; I left that out of the story because it conflicts with every other source. Missouri Life (403) and Living New Deal (not read) were not used. The Facebook post in search results was not read. No photos added.
